title: slicer land should accept --render, and show --json ready should agree with next
lead: `slicer land` accepts `--render` as a no-op, since it always renders. Plain `next --json`, `next --ready` and both `--batch` forms put the same `ready` value on each item as `show --json` and `list --json`, so an agent can see that `next` picked an item whose spec check was never recorded.
findings_note: squalify relay log 2026-10-27: 'slicer land' rejects --render unlike other mutations; 'slicer show ID --json' reported ready:false for a slice that list and next treated as ready (sq-16, 2026-10-26).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** making `next --ready` filter out items that are not ready-checked (it orders, by design); renaming the `ready` field or the `--ready` flag; `land --check` or `--strict` (land always runs check and gates its render; add them only if the owner asks); any change to how readiness goes stale.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Two independent concerns from one relay log (findings: squalify, sq-16, 2026-10-26/27). They stay one slice because both touch src/slicer/cli.py, docs/commands.md, docs/agents.md and CHANGELOG.md, and each is a few lines; they share no function. Split into two rows if the owner prefers.

Verified against main at 50bd033 on 2026-11-02:

1. `land` rejects `--render`. Its parser (src/slicer/cli.py:4517-4521) takes `id`, `--branch`, `--note` and `--owner` only; argparse refuses `--render` as unrecognized (exit 2). Yet `land.land` always runs `ops.done_and_render` and `cmd_land` always runs `_post_check` (cli.py:3191-3205; docs/landing.md:25 "Then it runs `done --render --check`"). `done`, `start`, `handoff` and the other mutations take `--render`, so an agent landing with the habit `--render` hits a usage error for a flag whose effect land already has.
2. "show --json ready disagrees with next": `show --json` and `list --json` add `ready` from `ops.ready_state` (cli.py:2375, 2646, 2655). It means a recorded spec check (`slicer ready ID --by NAME`): `true`, `false` (never checked, or no slice) or `"stale"`, as documented in docs/agents.md:962-970 and the `show` row of docs/commands.md:45. `next --ready` does not filter on it. It "lists `ready: true` items first within their tier and declared pass ... and drops nothing" (`ops._ready_first`, ops.py:1973-1991), so it can return an item whose `ready` is `false`. The `next --ready` item object (`_ready_entry`, cli.py:1921-1940: `id`, `title`, `status`, `depends_on`, `attempts`, notes, `effective_score`, `path`) and the plain `next` object (`_next_fields`, cli.py:1851-1864: `item.to_dict()`, `path`, `effective_score`) carry no `ready` at all. A reader then sees `next` hand over an item while `show` says `ready: false`, and nothing in the `next` payload explains it. The data never disagreed: the two commands use the word for different things, and only one says which. The fix is to report the same value on `next` and to say in the `--ready` help that it orders rather than filters. I could not see the sq-16 session itself; this reading comes from the code and docs.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py`:
  - `land` parser: wrap with `_render_flag` and give the flag help such as "accepted for symmetry with done; land always renders and checks". `cmd_land` ignores `args.render`.
  - `_ready_entry`: add `"ready": ops.ready_state(state, item)` to the item object directly after `"status"`.
  - `_next_fields`: add `"ready"` to the payload after `effective_score`.
  - `next --ready` help (cli.py:4271-4273): add that it does not filter, so the item's `ready` can be `false`.
  The `ready` key goes in a fixed position (deterministic output) and is kept under `--lean`, as `show --lean` keeps `false` today.
- `docs/commands.md`: the `land` row (line 88) gains `[--render]` and one clause saying it is accepted and changes nothing. The `next` row says items carry `ready`.
- `docs/agents.md`: the readiness paragraph (~line 962) says `next` (plain, `--ready`, `--batch`) also adds `ready`. The `next` JSON row (~line 601) names the key.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` `### Changed`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Land_RenderFlag_IsAcceptedAndChangesNothing` (tests/test_land.py, using that file's merged-branch fixture): `land ID --branch B --note N --render --json` exits 0 with the same payload keys and the same item status and written render files as without the flag. Fails today (exit 2, unrecognized argument).
- `test_NextReady_ItemCarriesReadyLikeShow` (tests/test_readiness.py): for an item never checked, checked, and checked then edited, `next --ready --json` `item.ready` equals `show ID --json` `ready` (`false`, `true`, `"stale"`), and the key comes right after `status`. Fails today (no key).
- `test_Next_PlainAndBatch_CarryReady` (tests/test_readiness.py): plain `next --json` and `next --batch 2 --json`, with and without `--ready`, carry `ready` on each item equal to `show`'s. Fails today.
- `test_NextReadyHelp_SaysItDoesNotFilter`: `next --help` text, whitespace-normalised, says `--ready` does not filter.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them fail.
2. Add `--render` to `land`; add `ready` to `_ready_entry` and `_next_fields`; update the `--ready` help.
3. Docs rows and paragraph, CHANGELOG. `tests/test_docs_coverage.py` checks that `--render` is named in the `land` row.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -k '*Land*'`, `-k '*NextReady*'`, `-k '*Readiness*'` and `-k '*DocsCoverage*'` (or `test_docs_coverage`) pass.
- [ ] `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer next --ready --json --lean` shows `ready` on the item, equal to `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer show <that id> --json --lean` `ready`.
- [ ] `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer land --help` lists `--render`.
- [ ] `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, the full suite, `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.
